interface.name: aqueous_output_warming_manager_v1
interface.description: Observation is not authorization. Only an acquired lease can request warming, and every request is checked again at real output submission. The protocol is available in all builds. Warming requires a supported live SDR renderer path; advertisement alone does not establish eligibility. Objects are connection scoped. Destroying this manager leaves its children alive. Security-context clients cannot bind this global.

interface.name: aqueous_output_warming_output_v1
interface.description: state followed by done is one snapshot. Tokens are unsigned 64-bit high/low pairs. Identity is session plus instance. Generation never rolls backward; reconnect/removal invalidates the object. Revision orders all state updates. Unknown reasons or encodings must be treated as unavailable. Acquire requires the generation from a completed snapshot.

interface.name: aqueous_output_warming_lease_v1
interface.description: acquired or denied answers acquisition. Denied and revoked leases are inert but must be destroyed. set and release IDs are nonzero, strictly increasing uint32 values; reuse is a protocol error. Each accepted ID gets one terminal result while the resource exists. New queued values supersede older ones. 2500..6500 K uses algorithm 1: linear RGB gains (1, 1-0.25*t, 1-0.65*t), t=(6500-K)/4000, followed by baseline gamma22 encoding. This parameter is not a measured white point. 6500 is neutral. committed means a successful backend commit, not physical color accuracy or presentation. Commit sequence is informational and may wrap. release completes only after baseline commits. Destroy/disconnect requests the same restoration without an acknowledgment. Failures may leave the previous committed value visible; observe output state for restoration.
